claims.statement: The environment configuration file `src/environments/environment.ts` contains the `apiUrl` (must be a valid `*.restheart.com` URL) and feature flags (`emailRegistration`, `passwordReset`, `oauthLogin`, `oauthProviders`, `teamInvitations`) that control which auth flows are available.
The rhc CLI workflow uses `rhc login`, `rhc setup --srv <srvId> --dry-run` (checks only), and `rhc setup --srv <srvId>` (apply changes) to configure the RESTHeart Cloud service.

The basic setup file `rhc.setup.ts` configures the accounts plugin, derives server feature flags from `environment.features`, sets Google OAuth credentials (when enabled) using `fromEnv()`, and manages the origin allowlist.

The consents setup file `rhc.setup.consents.ts` extends the basic setup with: user schema validation, users collection validation, consents permission (mergeRequest), JWT claims for `latestConsents/tos` and `latestConsents/pp`, and a Guards rule (451 blocking).

Version strings `TOS_VERSION` and `PP_VERSION` are defined once in `rhc.setup.consents.ts` and must agree in three places: the setup file, the Guards rule condition, and the public HTML files (`public/terms.html`, `public/privacy.html`).
The design system in `src/styles.css` is structured in five sections: design tokens (CSS custom properties), reset & base, skin classes, utility classes, and page scaffolds.
Light/dark mode is implemented via a `useTheme()` hook in `src/pages/shell/Shell.tsx` that persists preference to `localStorage` under key `rh-theme` and toggles the `dark` class on `<html>`.
The build workflow uses `npm run dev` for development (Vite with HMR), `npm run build` for production (tsc -b + vite build), and produces static files in `dist/` for deployment to any static hosting.
Page-specific CSS files under `src/pages/` contain only page-specific layout; all design tokens and shared styles live in `src/styles.css`.
